British Values
We promote British Values at SPSM through our teaching and expectations. Children learn about Democracy by knowing that their opinions and views matter and by respecting others' views. At SPSM we help children to understand the Rule of Law by being integral in the creation of school and classroom rules and learning that their actions have consequences and understanding right from wrong. We encourage children to develop self-knowledge and self-esteem through a range of experiences and activities and therefore, develop responsibility and a sense of Individual Liberty. Our diverse school teaches children how to share, be patient and challenge stereotypes, Mutual Respect and Tolerance.

Online Safety for Parents / Carers
Parent / Carers' Guides for Online Safety
We are proud to be a National Online Safety certified school and we know that children love being online. The internet is a fun, exciting, sociable and engaging place. However, the internet also has its dangers. Young people seem to be rich in knowledge surrounding technology and it can be difficult to keep track as our children explore the online world.
Whatever they are doing, our parent guides (updated regularly) will help you keep your children safe as they navigate the online world. Share these guides with your children. Start an online safety conversation today.
Parental Controls Set up Information
Parent / Carer Guide - Social Media and Mental Health
Over 30% of children subscribe to a social media account, despite many of them being below the age threshold. Social media gives children access to so much content and some of this content is not helpful for our young people's mental health and wellbeing. This means that it is vitally important that trusted adults know what children are consuming. Young people are attracted to these sites and content can be enthralling so it is up to us to ensure they are taking care of their wellbeing and being mindful of the content they access - especially knowing what to do if they see something they know is upsetting or not acceptable. Our guide is useful to support setting screen limits and how to restrict content children might access.
Online Safety for Parents / Carers
14 Ways to be Kind Online
Openview Education Information
SPSM have previously worked with Openview Education on different projects such as Anti-Bullying Week and Online Safety Week. They have been kind enough to share their new videos with us. These videos will help to begin discussions between you and your child around staying safe online, anti-bullying and wellbeing.
How to Clean Devices - Advice and Tips
We are all aware (especially given the current circumstances) how important it is to be aware of cleanliness and personal hygiene. We have much advice about hand washing but it is also important that we think carefully about how we clean and disinfect surfaces and objects. Not many people are aware that this is especially important with our electronic devices. Take a look at our guide to cleaning devices (and some 'dos' and 'don'ts).

PE and Sport Premium
Sports Clubs at SPSM
Here at SPSM we offer a varied range of extra-curricular school sporting activities. We aim to encourage and develop team work skills, an understanding of health and wellbeing, and also new and fun experiences. Although our swimming provision did not happen over Lockdown, we hope to be able to begin to provide this and as a result, publish children's attainment in swimming again very soon.
We cover a host of activities from taekwondo, to gymnastics, table tennis to street dance. Our sports clubs include children of all abilities from the nursery to year 6.
The sports provided by SPSM have gained us a silver status school award, as well as many of our young people competing in London youth games and borough wide competitions. Our successes are available for all to see in our well filled trophy cabinet!
Our team of sports staff are all qualified in their area of expertise and dedicated to delivering high quality sports activities to support the needs of all children, ensuring a very inclusive understanding of children who require additional support.
Sports clubs are applied for on a termly basis with pupil voice at the forefront of the selection of activities. Please look out for any updates. We look forward to seeing your child at one of our clubs soon!

Science & DT
Science is all around us! At SPSM we want our children to have a love for learning. We believe that Science should develop curiosity and perseverance as well as challenging what we know about the world. We aim to link Science to real life contexts and give meaning to our learning.
Our Science curriculum is:
Relevant and Engaging - real life opportunities for learning are included in all year groups. Children learn through investigations and experiments which spark their interest.
Active for Learning - we encourage children to think as scientists and make their own observations and conclusions.
Link making - by making Science relevant, children make links between their scientific knowledge and everyday life. We ensure that current affairs and scientific thinking is woven into our teaching.
Vocabulary Rich - we encourage use of high-level scientific vocabulary when talking and writing about our world.
Challenging - all children are challenged through questioning and content.
Ambitious for All - we aim to spark and develop curiosity about natural phenomena in all children and allow the to develop their own interests.
Cross-Curricular - we recognise the link between Science and all other subjects. Our lessons include a variety of extended writing, data analysis and other cross-curricular links.

History & Geography
History and Geography
At St Paul's with St Michael's we teach history and geography through topics. These topics link with our literacy, DT and art projects. Our geography and history teaching aims to equip our children with a working knowledge of local, national and international landscapes and a clear and coherent understanding of British and global history, and how this relates to us as compassionate and thankful members of society. By teaching our children to ask relevant questions, develop their perspective and judgement skills, we aim to ensure their skills to identify the challenges of our times and how to effectively overcome these with endurance as they develop as individuals.
Our end of topic projects consist of presentations, quizzes and essays. This develops our children's articulation and presentation skills, as well as improving their stamina for writing.
We use many local and further afield amenities to support our teaching. Hands on visits and activities enable the children to place events and places in context. Our topic curriculum has been designed to celebrate and respect the many wonderful and diverse cultures and influences we have in Hackney. Please see below for our topic overview for teaching and learning.

Reception - Early Years Team
Early Years Team Reception - Autumn Term 1, 2026.
Welcome to Reception.
Our topic this term is 'Myself' and we will be talking about ourselves, our families, where we live and people around us. Please talk to your children about your family members and other important people in their lives. Also, please bring in a family picture for your child to share with the class. You can send these digitally via the school admin email.
Please encourage your child to develop a love of reading by sharing books together each day. This makes for a great part of a bedtime routine. You can talk about the stories you read and ask your child to make predictions about what might happen next or look for clues in the pictures. This is an excellent opportunity to develop listening, attention and speaking skills.
Reception is an important year for children in terms of them gaining more independence, please support your children to try things for themselves. For instance, getting dressed and undressed, putting on or taking off their coats and shoes.
It is important that children come to school dressed in the correct uniform and that all belongings have names labelled. Children will need a spare set of clothes that they can keep in school in case of accidents.
Please return book bags every Tuesday and Friday so that books can be changed. PE will take place every Friday and children will need to bring their PE kit which consists of black bottoms, a white t-shirt and black trainers. All children are expected to complete their homework on a weekly basis. Homework is given on a Friday and needs to be returned by the following Friday. Your child will be given a 'Mathletics' and 'Reading Eggs' logon and password (you will find these in reading record logs). Certificates for achievement are awarded in our awards assembly each Friday.
Show and tell - your child will be learning a new sound each week. Please support your child by bringing an object or picture relating to the sound of the week. The sound we are working on will be displayed on the classroom door.
If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to speak to a member of the Reception Class Team.

Rights Respecting Schools
Rights Respecting Articles
The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child states what every child around the world should have access to or be able to engage with. SPSM agree with the UN that every child should know their rights and have these. Join SPSM on our journey to becoming a 'Rights Respecting School', take a look poster below (a larger version is also linked) - see what your rights are (you can also learn more by using the UN link added below)!
We are also very proud of our support for others to maintain their rights in different countries across the World. We raised money for the charity 'One Nation' who use donations to provide clean water through pumps and wells in countries where there is no access to clean water. Take a look at our link for more information.
Inauguration of 'Rights Respecting Ambassadors' and 'Eco-Warriors'
Our RR Ambassadors and Eco-Warriors made pledges to promote children's rights and care for our planet. They sealed their promises and started their special ambassadorial journeys during a special inauguration in front of the whole school.

School Governors are people who want to make a positive contribution to children's education.
